name: Lael
title: Leader of the Gershonites from the tribe of Levi
summary: Lael was the father of Elzaphan, who led the Gershonite clan within the tribe of Levi during Israel's wilderness journey. He is mentioned only once in the Bible, in connection with the census and organization of the Levites at Sinai. His name means 'belonging to God' or 'dedicated to God'.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the muster of the Levites
keyEvents.description: Lael is named as the father of Elzaphan, who was head of the Gershonite clan, in connection with the mustering of the Levites at Mount Sinai.

keyEvents.title: Tasks of the Gershonites at the tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Lael's son Elzaphan led the Gershonites, who were responsible for the tabernacle coverings, the curtain at the entrance, the hangings of the courtyard, and the ropes—all related to service at God's dwelling.

keyEvents.title: Camp location of the Gershonites
keyEvents.description: Under the leadership of Elzaphan, Lael's son, the Gershonites camped behind the tabernacle, toward the west, as part of the ordered camp structure around the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: Selection of the Levites in place of the firstborn
keyEvents.description: Lael belonged to the tribe of Levi, which was chosen by God to serve in place of all the firstborn in Israel, an important arrangement established at Sinai.
